name: Tur Suil
summary: Balor's tower on Hy Brasil, raised by the Fomorians around the eye that would not close.

facts.text: Tur Suil's bestiary: Balor (81), Queen Qunilaria, Norsob the Annihilator, Sargan the Conqueror, Kierac the Destroyer, the Master of Pain, Abomos the Soultrapper, the Balorians, spectral and tortured Sylvan spirits, burrowing monstrosities, tunneling horrors, wall spikes and a rack of spikes.
The Balorians bear old Irish hero names: Conall, Ferdiad, Conlaoch, Aonghus, Donogh, Huon, Sluaghan, Meisceoir and others.
Region 190; the realm raid's final is Balor. The Vale of Balor is a zone of Hy Brasil (region 181).
Shrouded Isles set the Fomorians against the Sylvan of Hy Brasil, who asked Hibernia for help.

Balor, Fomorian king, had an eye that destroyed what it looked on; his grandson Lugh killed him at the second battle of Mag Tuired; folklore sets his tower on Tory Island, where he shut away his daughter.
A Dec 2003 Balor raid: 'you only need 2fg's'; the raid brought three groups.
Bot chat: his eye once opened over Hy Brasil and burned the valley now called the Vale of Balor; never meet his eye.
Tur Suil may be Irish túr súl, 'tower of the eye'; to verify.
Tur Suil's raid is dungeon-hibernia-tursuil, suggested size 40; its entrance in the navigation data is at 38038, 27675.
Every Tur Suil named takes 20-30% less from slash, crush and thrust and cannot be hurt outside its tether.
Allakhazam lists a Rack of Spikes at level 99 and Wall Spikes at level 90 in Tur Suil: traps, not foes.
Folklore says Balor shut his daughter Eithne in a tower on Tory Island so that the prophecy of his death by his grandson could not come true.

story:
Every child in Hibernia knows how Balor died. Lugh, his own grandson, put a sling-stone through the terrible eye at Mag Tuired and drove it out through the back of the king's skull, and it fell looking at the Fomorian host and burned them where they stood. The bards end the tale there. The Fomorians did not.

They gathered what was left, the Sylvan say: the eye, still open, still burning, wrapped in seven hides and carried by men who walked backwards. They took it west, to the isle that nobody could find, and when it opened once on the way a whole valley of Hy Brasil turned to ash. On a crag above that valley they built a tower to hold it, as Balor had once built a tower to hold his daughter, and around the eye, over long years, they grew their king back. Tur Suil, the tower of the eye. The Balor who sits in it now is the eye's own idea of a king.

His household fills the tower. His soldiers carry the names of heroes the Fomorians once killed, worn like trophies. His soul-trapper keeps the spirits of the Sylvan who tried to burn the tower, and keeps them screaming. His torturer has filled the walls with spikes, and his burrowers dig ever downward, toward the roots of the isle. And in the highest room the king waits, and every wound he takes opens another eye somewhere in the dark, looking for whoever gave it.

What lives there now is a household. At the gate and on the long stair stand the Balorians, the king's soldiers, each wearing the name of a hero the Fomorians once killed: Conall, Ferdiad, Conlaoch, Aonghus, Huon, Maccus. Sargan gave them those names, so that every soldier would be a trophy, and the Hibernians who climb the stair try not to read them aloud. Bugbear scavengers pick through what the soldiers leave. The walls are set with spikes, and in the torturer's hall stands a rack the Allakhazam scholars rated at a level no warrior has ever reached; it is not a foe, it is furniture. Spectral Sylvan drift in the lower halls, and tortured Sylvan spirits cry behind the walls of the soul-trapper's cells. Far below, the burrowing monstrosities and tunneling horrors of Queen Qunilaria's brood dig ever down, toward the roots of the isle, toward whatever the king hopes to find there.

Each of the great ones keeps a hall. Norsob holds the west, Sargan the far west; they hate each other and Balor keeps them apart on purpose. Kierac the Destroyer guards the torturer's hall without knowing what he carries inside him. Abomos keeps the cells. Qunilaria keeps the nest. And at the top of the crag, in the chamber with one window, sits the king. Every one of them is hard-skinned against blades, every one of them is bound to its own hall and cannot be harmed beyond it, as if the tower would not let its household be wounded anywhere but at their posts.

Why does it matter? Because of the Vale. The valley below the crag is ash where the eye looked on it once, and the Sylvan cannot forget that the eye could look again. When the Sylvan came to Hibernia for swords it was Tur Suil they named first, before Fomor, before anything. And there is the older reason. Every Hibernian child learns the tale of Mag Tuired, of Lugh's sling and the falling eye, and every Hibernian child grows up thinking it ended there. Tur Suil is the realm's proof that it did not. A raid that climbs the tower and brings the king down is, in the bards' eyes, finishing a story that Lugh began.
legend: Two or three groups if they are good. Never stand where the eyes can see you all at once: every tenth of his health another Eye of Balor opens over the room and burns whoever it looks at. Kill fast, spread out, heal through the light. Clear the queen and the warlords first, and mind the spikes in the walls. Nicknames: 'the Eye', 'the one-window tower', and for Balor himself 'Grandad', because of Lugh, which the old hibs think is in poor taste. Superstitions: never read the Balorians' names aloud; never look up through the window of the king's chamber; carry a smooth stone in your pack for luck, as Lugh did. Raid leaders say two or three groups is enough, but bring a fourth for the stair.

firstEntry: The tower of the eye. Do not look up.
The walls are full of spikes, and the spikes are full.
Somewhere above, a lid is lifting.
The soldiers wear the names of dead heroes.
A tower with one window. Something looks out.
Somewhere below, digging, and it does not stop.

loremaster.intro: Tur Suil, the tower of the eye. You know how [Balor] died at Mag Tuired, and who his grandson [Lugh] was. Ask instead what became of the [eye], and why the [Vale] below the crag is ash. The Fomorians built this tower and filled it with [his household]: the [Balorians] on the stair, and his great ones in their halls.

topics.Balor: King of the Fomorians, whose single eye burned whatever it looked on. Lugh, his grandson, put it out with a sling-stone. Or so we sing.
topics.eye: It fell open and burned the Fomorian host. They wrapped it in hides and carried it west, walking backwards, and it opened once on Hy Brasil. That valley is the Vale of Balor now.
topics.his household: Soldiers wearing the names of our dead heroes; a soul-trapper; a torturer called the [Master of Pain]; two warlords; and a queen of burrowing things.
topics.Master of Pain: He lived inside Kierac the Destroyer, the Sylvan say, as a worm lives in an apple. Kill Kierac and he comes out.
topics.Balorians: The king's soldiers, named by [Sargan] for heroes the Fomorians killed. Do not read the names aloud.
topics.Vale: The valley below the crag, ash since the eye looked on it. The Sylvan named Tur Suil first when they asked for swords.
topics.Lugh: Balor's grandson, who put a sling-stone through the eye at Mag Tuired. Carry a smooth stone into the tower for luck.
topics.Eithne: In the old tale, Balor's daughter, shut in a tower so the prophecy could not come true. It came true. Towers do not hold everything.

book.title: The Tower of the Eye
pages: Written by Muirgen, a druid of Tir na Nog who went to Hy Brasil with the first of the realm's swords. The bards sing that Lugh drove the eye of Balor out through the back of his head, and that it fell facing the Fomorian host, and that their own king's gaze destroyed them. The Sylvan of Hy Brasil have a second verse. They say the Fomorians who lived were the ones who had been walking backwards, as the eye's bearers always walked, and that they wrapped the eye in seven hides of seven beasts and carried it to the sea without once turning round.

The Sylvan say the boat came to Hy Brasil in a mist, as all boats come there, and that the hides slipped on the shore. The eye looked at one valley for as long as it takes to draw breath. Nothing has grown there since; the Sylvan call it by Balor's name now, and walk round it. The Fomorians built a tower on the crag above it, a tower with one window, as Balor in the old tale built a tower on Tory to shut his daughter away. They put the eye behind the window, and they began, slowly, to grow a king around it again.

The household came after. A soul-trapper for the Sylvan raiders who came to burn the tower. A torturer, already dead, who filled the walls with spikes and lived inside the best thing he ever made. Two warlords who could not stand each other, kept in separate halls. A queen of burrowing things, set to dig. And soldiers, many soldiers, given the names of heroes the Fomorians had killed, so that every one of them is a boast. I counted the names on the stair and stopped at forty. I will not write them here.

When Hibernia's raids first climbed to the top of Tur Suil they found him there: Balor, or what the eye remembers of Balor. He bleeds, and he can die. But every tenth part of his strength that falls opens another eye somewhere in the room, high up where no sword can reach, and each eye burns. The raiders learned to stand apart and heal through the light. One of them, a young bard, carried a smooth stone in his pack all the way up, for Lugh's sake. He told me afterward he had not needed it. He had been glad of it anyway.

A note in another hand, beside these pages in the library at Tir na Nog: the eye was never his. He was always the eye's. I believe that is right. In the old tale the prophecy said Balor would die by his grandson, and he shut his daughter in a tower, and it did not help. Towers do not hold everything. The Fomorians built another tower for the eye, and filled it with soldiers, and set a queen to dig beneath it. I do not think it will help them either. But I think we will have to keep climbing it, every generation, to make sure.
